title: Context fusion notes — lab + reading digest
content:
Purpose: quick brain dump after reading a few papers and doing a tiny local spike. Goal is to capture intuition, next experiments, and a sketch we can demo for the runtime team.

---

Reading digest (high level takeaways)

1) "Context Fusion for Episodic Retrieval" (paper notes) — gist: treat retrieved chunks and KV cache entries as orthogonal channels, fuse with a learned gating layer at attention time rather than concatenation.
   - Key idea: small learned projector that maps retrieval vectors -> attention biases; cheaper than attending over retrieval tokens every step.
   - Why it matters: could cut per-token cost for long RAG flows while preserving signal from longer documents.
   - Caveat: extra trainable parameters and need for aligned embedding space.

2) "Gradient-efficient Locality Compression" (workshop blog) — gist: lossy compression for KV caches that preserves top-k nearest neighbors via product quantization + learned residuals.
   - Tradeoffs: good for memory pressure on Dedicated, needs benchmarking on different model sizes (7B vs 34B).
   - Ops note: decompression cost sometimes outweighs mem savings at low-latency SLOs. Measure decompression microsecond budget.

3) "Adaptive Eviction Policies for Long-term Cache" (conference talk notes) — gist: eviction based on a combined score: recency * retrieval usefulness * freshness score from user-signal (explicit feedback).
   - Practical: simple TTL + LRU baseline wins a lot; more complex policies need good telemetry to beat baseline.

---

Micro-spike summary (local experiment Sep 16)

Setup: tiny toy server (cpu-limited) with a 3M vector store (dense), and a mocked KV cache with compressed vectors. Ran synthetic chat sessions with repeated topics (support tickets) to test hit-rate and latency.

Findings (raw):
- naive fusion (concat(retrieved + kv tokens)) increased p50 token latency by ~18% on my laptop.
- bias-fusion (project retrieval -> attention bias) increased generation quality in QA prompts measurably (ROUGE-ish proxy) with only ~3% latency overhead.
- PQ compression saved ~55% mem, but decompress cost added 0.6ms per token on avg; on Dedicated GPUs that may be fine, not for hosted small-instances.

Next hypotheses to validate:
- H1: bias-fusion generalizes across sequence lengths (<=1024 and 4096) without more than 5% quality drop.
- H2: compressed-KV + caching of decompressed blocks reduces decompression tax for repeated access patterns (hot blocks).

Experiment plan (concrete)
- Dataset: 2k simulated sessions (support + legal + onboarding), plus Evals set of 200 prompts for subjective quality checks.
- Metrics: p50/p95 token latency, tokens/sec, retrieval hit-rate, mean answer fidelity (BLEU/ROUGE proxy), cost-per-1000-tokens estimate.
- Implementations to compare: baseline(RAG-concat), bias-fusion(project->bias), early-fusion(embedding average), and hybrid(online learned gate).
- Ramp: local (dev laptop) -> small GPU node (g4dn-ish) -> Dedicated pool w/ quantized kernel.

Engineering notes / integration points
- Runtime: need a hook in the attention builder to accept "attention_bias_from_retrieval" as an optional input. See runtime PR #987 for an initial shape API.
- Batching: ensure bias-fusion supports continuous batching; biases should be additive and compatible with per-request pad masks.
- Telemetry: add traces for retrieval vs kv-hit decisions, and surface decomposition time when compression used. New traces should map to the Console route-level dashboards.
- Rollout plan: feature flag at model-route level -> canary with 1% traffic -> 10% -> full. Add automatic fallback to RAG-concat if p95 latency > threshold.

Prompt templates (for evals)
- QA + context fusion check: "You are support assistant. Given the retrieved context and memory snippets, answer succinctly. If the context contradicts, say "I am not sure" and explain which snippet caused the contradiction."
- Fragment stitching probe: feed two retrieved fragments with slight overlap and ask model to identify contradictions and stitch into a single unified summary. Check hallucination rate.

Open questions / risks (notes to self)
- Alignment: does projecting retrieval into attention biases require training end-to-end with generation? Or can we freeze the LM and train only projector? (fast experimentation: train projector only on distilled teacher labels).
- Safety: fusion could surface private user info from long-term store more easily. Need filters/token-level redaction policy.
- Cost math: need unit-cost model comparing extra projector (tiny but persistent) vs increased token attention work. Build a per-route calculator in Optimize.
- Metrics: how to measure "usefulness" for eviction policy offline without user feedback? Proxy: downstream model perplexity delta when entry is removed. Costly but informative.

TODOs (short)
- [ ] Add microbenchmark harness that instruments decompression time per block (RED-4123).
- [ ] Prototype projector-only distillation on 7B model with frozen LM (Aisha agreed to help).
- [ ] Post a short write-up to eng-kv-cache channel with p95 numbers and two plots.
- [ ] Sync with runtime cats (PT) about attention hook shape — schedule 30min next Tue.

Links referenced / quick bibliography
- internal spike: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Context+Fusion+Spike
- runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987
- related blog: https://example.ai/blog/gradient-local-compression (bookmark for PQ details)

Random scribbles / ideas to keep:
- Could we opportunistically fuse only when retrieval confidence > threshold? saves cost.
- Track per-query "fusion value" by computing offline delta in model-specified utility; surface top talkers in Console.
- Consider a tiny LUT to map doc-type -> fusion-weight (legal docs might get stronger fusion).

End of dump. Will tidy into a short one-pager if any of the experiments show wins.

Notes date: 2026-09-20.
